messages:
Anya: quick proposal — add a compact provenance vector to rollout metadata so ops can trace why a specific variant was chosen. see mini-RFC gist: https://example.com/rfc/provenance-vector
Samir: what do you mean by 'compact'? worried about blowup in telemetry and request headers
Anya: compact = signed, base64-encoded token (opaque to clients) + optional small human labels array. token holds lineage hash, signer id, timestamp, and an optional confidence score. runtime stores token in request metadata (not in user-visible payload).
Cleo: +1 on opaque token. two practical questions: 1) where do we store signer keys? 2) can we cheaply verify token in low-latency paths if needed?
Anya: signer keys = KMS/HSM. verification is optional in hot path; most consumers will only log token and surface to debug UI. we can provide a verification endpoint for async checks.
Samir: fallback behavior? if token missing or invalid, how should routing behave?
Cleo: routing should be conservative: treat invalid/missing as 'unknown-provenance' and allow existing fallback rules (last-stable, tenant-overrides). we should not block inference on token failure.
Anya: draft metadata shape (keeps runtime cheap):
```json
{
  "provenance_token": "<base64-signed-blob>",
  "lineage_labels": ["staging-2026-03-20", "canary-3%"],
  "rollout_fidelity": "0.92",
  "rollback_hint": "last-stable:sha256:12ab34cd"
}
```
Cleo: nice. a couple of tradeoffs:
- token size vs observability: if we embed full chain, it grows quickly. instead store chain in control plane and keep token as a pointer+sig.
- privacy: token might accidentally include tenant ids; ensure tokens don't leak PII.
Samir: agree. also: metrics/telemetry cost — if we include labels per-request we'll increase cardinality. prefer storing token and only expanding when investigating.
Anya: plan then: provenance_token = pointer+sig (~128-256 bytes). control plane keeps full chain. lineage_labels are optional low-cardinality tags (max 3). runtime: store token in request metadata and in traces only when sampling.
Cleo: signing algorithm suggestion: ed25519 for small signature and fast verification. use KMS-backed keys with rotation metadata.
Samir: how does this interact with pin/evict logic? ops want to understand if a pin came from client intent, rollout policy, or auto-heal. can token carry a reason enum?
Anya: yes — include a small reason code in token payload (client_pin | autoscaler | canary_rollout | operator_override). that stays opaque unless decoded by control plane.
DeployBot: Deployment succeeded: model "staging-2026-03-20" -> variant v3 at 2026-03-20T10:00:00Z :rocket:
Cleo: next steps: prototype token format and a tiny verifier service; run a perf test with 1M sampled verifications to estimate cost.
Samir: I'll add a telemetry simulation to see cardinality impact if lineage_labels are attached to 1%/10%/100% of requests.
Anya: I'll open a short RFC PR with the token spec, examples, and ops playbook (how to query control plane for full chain). also will include migration guidance: conservative default = opt-in for 30 days, then flip to on-by-default for newly created rollouts.
Cleo: and add a CLI tool to decode a token with proper auth so SREs can quickly inspect without control-plane UI.
Anya: agreed. action items summarized: 1) Anya: RFC PR + migration plan. 2) Cleo: prototype signer/verifier + CLI. 3) Samir: telemetry sim. We'll reconvene after initial numbers. :+1:
